problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.000\,08$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
256,\,64,\,16,\,4,\,…
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.000\,31$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
125,\,25,\,5,\,1,\,…
$$

The first term that is less than $0.000\,31$ is the
{{field-1}}th term.
feedback.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=125$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{25}{125}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =125\cdot {(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} \\  & ={5}^{3}\cdot {5}^{1-n} \\  & ={5}^{4-n}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $0.000\,31.$
Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & <0.000\,31 \\ {5}^{4-n} & <0.000\,31 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({5}^{4-n}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,31) \\ (4-n)\operatorname{log}⁡(5) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,31) \\ 4-n & <\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,31)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)} \\ -n & <\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,31)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}-4 \\ n & >4-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,31)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get

$$
4-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,31)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}≈9.020.
$$

Therefore, the $10$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $0.000\,31.$
